title: Quick check: Configuration Files in Next.js

questions.prompt: In the context of “Configuration Files in Next.js” and “next.config.js”, In the App Router, which file convention supplies the UI for a route?
options: An arbitrary component file anywhere in the repository with no route export.
A `page.jsx` file inside the route’s folder.
questions.answer_key: A `page.jsx` file inside the route’s folder.
questions.explanation: The App Router uses reserved file conventions; `page.jsx` makes a route segment publicly accessible.

questions.prompt: While implementing “Configuration Files in Next.js”, What is the primary purpose of a `layout.jsx` file?
options: To store environment secrets for all pages.
To define shared UI that wraps child routes and can persist across navigation.
To define an HTTP endpoint for every request method.
To replace all route pages with one global component.
questions.answer_key: To define shared UI that wraps child routes and can persist across navigation.
questions.explanation: Layouts provide shared route-segment UI and preserve structure across eligible child navigations.

questions.prompt: When reviewing “Configuration Files in Next.js”, Where should database access and reusable domain rules generally live?
options: In the browser bundle with database credentials.
In clearly separated server/data-access modules rather than mixed into every page component.
questions.answer_key: In clearly separated server/data-access modules rather than mixed into every page component.
questions.explanation: Separating route files from trusted data access improves reuse and helps keep secrets out of client bundles.
